body:
@fritshoogland-yugabyte suggested setting  `/proc/<pid>/oom_adj` for postgres based on a recent experiment where we saw the OOM killer take down the tserver when a postgres process increased RSS. 

We can either wait for systemd integration in Platform and set this via systemd (https://askubuntu.com/questions/60672/how-do-i-use-oom-score-adj) or modify postgres code to set this on itself based on a conf setting maybe.

issue.title: [docdb] Add YSQL memory tracking into TS MemTracker

repository.name: yugabyte-db
repository.description: YugabyteDB - the cloud native distributed SQL database for mission-critical applications.

issue.body:
Jira Link: [DB-966](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-966)
On the tserver side, we use the MemTracker framework for both
1. Capturing total memory used, across components

For the first part, I was discussing with @spolitov, since PG uses processes for independent backends, we should be able to pull in data about how much memory each process uses, just from the operating system. This would be less granular than our usual MemTracker::Consume approach, but would at least allow us to get a high level view of how much memory we're using, on a node, across all PG backends.

We already use a callback based approach in the MemTracker, for the `root` node, to fetch external data from tcmalloc directly. We can reuse the same approach here.

2. Leverage that information to then reject new memory allocations

Here there's also 2 problems
- New connections will inevitably need more new memory
With this MemTracker integration, we might be able to then wire some polling back into the TS MemTracker and thus allow the PG master to reject new connections, if we've hit the memory limit!

- Existing connections might continue to need memory and grow their existing usage
This would be a bit harder with this coarse approach, as we don't have granular control. However, perhaps at that point, we could just let something like https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/issues/8494 kill the backends, as a worst case scenario?

issue.body:
Jira Link: [DB-1213](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-1213)
Currently, there are a couple of scenarios during which YB runs into various memory issues. These can manifest as
- OOM -- when to cumulative amount of memory on a server goes too high
- soft memory limit RPC rejections -- when an individual master/tserver runs into heap allocation issues with tcmalloc

### Stage 1 (improved cheap defaults)
✅ Reduce master memstore memory usage (#10242)
✅ Fix network buffer percentage calculation (#10207)
✅ Make global log cache use a percentage of total (#3745)

### Stage 2 (better management of tcmalloc internals)
✅ Periodically clear tcmalloc internals (#10243)
✅ Reduce master memory pressure due to tcmalloc free bytes (#11406)
✅ Reduce master memory pressure due to tcmalloc thread cache (#11398)

### Stage 3 (OOM prevention)
✅ Make OOM prioritize PG backends (#8494)

### Stage 4 (new memory management mechanics)
⬜️ Connect YSQL with the TS MemTracker framework (#10284)

### Description

Issue #8494 prevents the postmaster from restarting when a Postgress backend dies in a safe manner. This feature is turned off by default. This ticket aims at turning this off by default.
